unit.why: One continuous narrative about the end of the Besht's life: after his wife's death he refuses to remarry, and on the day of his death he takes leave of his son R. Zvi.
unit.boundary_note: Two linked episodes joined by 'וביום מותו'. They could be split as two anecdotes, but are treated here as one story.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי כשמתה אשתו של רבינו הקדוש
stories.summary_en: After his wife dies, the Besht refuses to remarry, saying he had been abstinent for fourteen years. On the day of his death his son R. Zvi, who did not believe his father would die, is woken and weeps. The Besht tells him of his holy soul, conceived when all the heavens trembled, and teaches him a holy name to concentrate on so that he may see his father and learn with him after his death.

tags.why: The central scene is the Besht's last day and his parting instructions to his son.

tags.why: Contemplative concentration on a divine name.
Esoteric knowledge of soul impregnation (ibbur) and of divine names is transmitted.
Drawing down Adam's soul through ibbur is mentioned as a possibility.
The Besht foretells his own death that day.
A deathbed testament to the son, though no succession is stated.
The wife is referred to but does not act.
